figures.caption: Figure 1: Uncertainty-aware and scale-invariant directional transfer learning via angular cone prior. (1) Source coefficient distribution in (β1, β2) space. (2) Corresponding directional distribution on S1 under the mapping T (β) = β/∥β∥2, with mean direction µs. (3) Angular cone prior centered at µs, encouraging directional alignment while decoupling magnitude estimation.

Figure 2: Prediction risk under heterogeneous directional source information. Assume that the directional distribution of the source coefficient is bi-modal. The horizontal axis varies the angular separation between source directional components, while the vertical axis varies the proportion of source mass assigned to the direction aligned with the target signal. (a) Risk of point-wise transfer, which increases as source directions become more separated due to averaging across conflicting signals. (b) Risk of the proposed distributional transfer estimator, which remains comparatively stable by aggregating over multiple plausible source directions. (c) Relative gain of DUST over point-wise transfer, showing the largest improvement in regimes with heterogeneous yet partially informative source structure. Lower values indicate better predictive performance.
Table 1: Linear regression (directional transfer under unimodal heterogeneous source structure). Mean test MSE with standard error in parentheses (lower is better).
Table 2: Linear model (directional transfer under bimodal source heterogeneity). Mean test MSE with standard error in parentheses (lower is better).
Table 3: Logistic regression (directional transfer under unimodal heterogeneous source structure). Mean test log-loss with standard error in parentheses (lower is better).
Table 4: Logistic regression (directional transfer under bimodal source heterogeneity). Mean test log-loss with standard error in parentheses (lower is better).
Table 6: Poisson regression. Test MSE on the linear predictor with standard error in parentheses (lower is better).
Table 7: Quantile regression (τ = 0.5). Test pinball loss with standard error in parentheses (lower is better).
